visual_action: Musician Bad Bunny accepts an award on stage at the Grammy Awards. He gives a speech at a podium, holding the award statue. The video cuts between close-ups of him, wider shots of the stage, and shots of the audience applauding enthusiastically.

cast.name: Bad Bunny
cast.evidence: On-screen text identifies him as 'Bad Bunny' and he is the sole speaker in the video.

cast.name: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)
cast.evidence: The speaker says 'I'm going to say ICE out,' which is also displayed in on-screen text.

on_screen_text.text: Bad Bunny at the Grammys: Before I say thanks to God, I’m going to say ICE out.
BEST MÚSICA URBANA ALBUM DEBÍ TIRAR MÁS FOTOS BAD BUNNY

spoken_summary: In an acceptance speech, Bad Bunny says that before he thanks God, he is going to say 'ICE out.' After a long pause for applause, he continues, 'We're not savage, we're not animals, we're not aliens. We are humans, and we are Americans.' The word 'aliens' is spoken but not included in the on-screen captions.
audio_music: Live audio from an awards show. The primary sound is the speaker's voice, followed by a long and loud period of cheering and applause from the audience. There is no musical score.
editing_pacing: Standard event coverage style, with cuts between a close-up on the speaker, wider shots of the stage, and reaction shots of the applauding audience. The shots are mostly static.
central_claim: Prominent cultural figures like Bad Bunny are using their platforms at major events like the Grammys to denounce ICE and advocate for immigrant rights, a message that is met with widespread applause.
intended_effect: To align the Democratic party with a popular celebrity's pro-immigrant stance and to make viewers feel proud and inspired by this public display of solidarity.
